figures.caption: Figure 1: Pretrained EFM embeddings amplify subject information. Frozen CBraMod embeddings improve linear subject probing over raw EEG and form subject-dependent clusters. Task probes use subject-disjoint splits; subject probes use held-out trials from known subjects.

Figure 2: Overview: motivation and empirical effect of DEFT. Left: standard EFM fine-tuning leaves the classifier to suppress subject-related variation inside mixed pretrained tokens, while DEFT models subject-consistent information before classification. Right: an illustrative Balanced Accuracy snapshot across representative datasets and foundation models, showing that DEFT improves over vanilla fine-tuning in most displayed comparisons.

Figure 3: Overall framework of DEFT. Mixed pretrained tokens are organized into task-content and subject-style branches, then optimized with temporal-variance regularization, classification, subject-aware contrastive learning, and reconstruction. The downstream classifier uses the content branch for prediction. Detailed processes of each stage are shown above the overall framework.

Table 1: Main results on six representative downstream datasets. All metrics report multi-seed mean±std over available seeds. Bold marks the best value in each metric column, and Delta is the absolute improvement of DEFT over vanilla fine-tuning. Chance B-ACC is 0.250, 0.111, 0.200, 0.500, 0.333, and 0.500 for BCIC-IV-2a, FACED, ISRUC-S1, MentalArith., BCIC-Speech, and Mumtaz2016, respectively.

Figure 4: Representation geometry before and after disentanglement. Top: subject-controlled within-subject class separation after subject centering, where higher values indicate clearer class structure within each subject. Bottom: class t-SNE visualizations of the same before-module and content-branch representations.
Table 3: Compute accounting for reproducing the reported experiments. All values are approximate.
Table 4: Dataset sources and usage terms for the complete evaluation suite.
Table 5: Dataset shapes, class counts, task types, and split statistics used in the reported experiments. Each dataset is shown with subject counts and sample counts in separate rows.
